rules.cost: Round-trip cost is at most 25% of the amount risked
rules.vol: Volume is at least 2x normal for this time of day (indices pass)
rules.mkt: Nifty is on the same side of its VWAP as the trade
rules.conf: No other strategy is already on the opposite side of the same stock today

strategies.name: Opening drive
strategies.best_for: A stock that opens and runs hard in the first 5 to 15 minutes on heavy volume, when waiting for a breakout means buying the high.
strategies.risk: A thrust that fades after the open, or a gap-and-fail. The stop is wide because it sits at the base of the move.
rules: Only in the first 15 minutes (candles closing 9:20 to 9:30).
The stock must already be up (or down) 1.5% or more from the open, on at least 3x its usual volume by this time.
The candle must close in the top 30% of its range (bottom 30% for a sell), on the right side of VWAP, still making a new high (or low) for the day.
Enter at that candle's close, near the start of the move. Stop at the base of the move (the low of the day so far for a buy).
No fixed target: the trade ends when a candle closes below the low of the last 3 candles (above the high for a sell), or at 3:15 pm.

Enter when a 5-minute candle closes outside the range, once per direction per day.
Stop at the opposite end of the range, target 1.5x the range height beyond the breakout.

strategies.name: EMA trend pullback
strategies.best_for: Established strong trends, bullish or bearish. The strategy only works when ADX is 22 or more.
strategies.risk: Missing the trade if the trend is too strong to ever pull back.
rules: The 20-period average must be above the 50-period (below it for sells), and the 50-period must be sloping the same way.
ADX must be at least 22, and price on the trend side of the 50-period average.
A candle dips to the 20-period average and closes back above it (below it for sells), in the trend's direction.
Stop half a typical candle range past the dip extreme, target 2x the risk. Exit early if price closes through the 50-period.

chronological_validation.warning: Too few sessions for a useful chronological split.

assumptions: Each trade risks about ₹500 on a share (position capped at ₹40,000) or one lot of an index future, so results are comparable between strategies.
Shares are bought or sold intraday. Index trades use the index level as a stand-in for the futures price.
Costs deducted: ₹40 plus 0.03% of turnover and 0.03% slippage per leg on shares; ₹80 plus 0.02% and 0.01% slippage per leg on index futures.
A signal is executed at the next five-minute candle open; a gap through the stop invalidates the trade.
Indicators use only past candles. Index volume does not exist, so volume checks are skipped for indices and their average price line is a plain average.
No setting was tuned to this data. Every number is the one set out on the strategy's tab.
All open trades are closed by 15:15.

Strategy tabs show standalone candidate results. The portfolio report separately applies TAKE-grade admission, one concurrent position per underlying, aggregate open-risk, position-count and daily-loss limits.
The chronological 60/20/20 split and stability blocks are diagnostic slices only; no parameter optimisation or untouched holdout is claimed.
Session-clustered t-statistics use daily average R to reduce trade-level dependence; they are descriptive, not proof of an edge.
